original_question: If one restricts numerical integration or approximation algorithms to use iid sample points, what tractability properties can still be achieved? More precisely, how should one characterize and prove tractability results for algorithms based on iid samples, and how do these iid tractability properties differ from the tractability of algorithms using optimally chosen information?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Open Problem after Remark 10: study iid tractability for algorithms based on iid sample points, and compare optimal versus iid sample points via tractability properties and asymptotic constants. The nearby paper context is Theorem 5.1, Theorem 5.2, Corollaries 1-2, together with the general information-complexity setup from Section 1 and the tractability notions from Section 2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the key unresolved theme of the paper's iid-sampling section: what survives when algorithms are forced to use iid sample points, and how that compares with algorithms using optimally chosen sampling information. It is also right to ask for tractability rather than only convergence rates, because the paper explicitly says that, after the optimal-order results in Section 5, the next issue is to study iid tractability. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))
missing_details: The paper's official open problem is not about arbitrary approximation/integration settings; it arises from the Section 5 problems, most explicitly L_q-approximation and numerical integration for Sobolev spaces W_p^s(Ω). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

The iid restriction is specific: the sampling points are realizations of independent random variables uniformly distributed on the domain Ω, not arbitrary iid laws. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

The domain assumptions are part of the setup: Ω ⊂ R^d is open and bounded and, in the main Section 5 framework, satisfies an interior cone condition; the comparison is explicitly allowed to depend on the dimension d and on the domain Ω. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

A stand-alone formulation should define tractability via the information complexity n(ε,d) from Section 1 and the notions stated in Section 2—at least curse of dimensionality, polynomial tractability, and strong polynomial tractability. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

Section 5 works with two different randomized error criteria, Monte Carlo error and uniform error, and the known iid-versus-optimal comparisons differ between them; a precise question should either fix one criterion or ask for both separately. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

Your phrase 'optimally chosen information' is slightly broader than the paper's nearby comparison, which is usually phrased in terms of optimally selected deterministic or random sampling points; the open problem itself asks about the difference between optimal and iid sample points. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

The paper's motivation is that optimal-order results are already known in Section 5, so the new question is explicitly about tractability and not about recovering those rates. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

The paper also proposes a concrete quantitative refinement: study asymptotic constants for the minimal iid errors and ask whether they exist and depend only on |Ω| rather than on the shape of Ω. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))
refined_question: For the approximation and integration problems treated in Section 5—most explicitly, the d-dimensional L_q-approximation problem id_d: W_p^s(Ω_d) → L_q(Ω_d) and the integration problem I_d(f) = ∫_{Ω_d} f on open, bounded domains Ω_d ⊂ R^d satisfying an interior cone condition, with Sobolev parameters in the regime where point evaluation is continuous—define the iid information complexity n_iid(ε,d) by restricting admissible randomized algorithms to operators of the form A_n(f) = φ(X_1, ..., X_n; f(X_1), ..., f(X_n)), where X_1, ..., X_n are iid and uniformly distributed on Ω_d. For each of the Monte Carlo and uniform error criteria used in Section 5, determine whether the resulting family of problems suffers from the curse of dimensionality or is polynomially or strongly polynomially tractable in the sense of Section 2, how these iid tractability properties depend on the problem type, the dimension d, and the domains Ω_d, how they compare with the corresponding tractability properties when the sampling points may be chosen optimally (deterministically or randomly), and whether the relevant asymptotic constants for the minimal iid errors exist and depend only on |Ω_d| rather than on the shape of Ω_d. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))
justification: The nearest official target is the Section 5 open problem on iid tractability, not Theorem 5.1 or Theorem 5.2 themselves. Those results, together with Corollaries 1-2, already establish optimal-order comparisons for iid uniformly distributed samples under the Monte Carlo and uniform error criteria; the open problem then explicitly says that one should study iid tractability and the difference between optimal and iid sample points, and it suggests asymptotic constants as one concrete way to do so. To make that open problem stand alone, one must import the paper's information-complexity setup from Section 1 and its tractability notions from Section 2, while keeping the Section 5 Sobolev/domain/iid-uniform sampling framework and the distinction between Monte Carlo and uniform errors. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))
